data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

actors.name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)
Associate CIO for Cyber Security (ACIO CS)
Agency Information Systems Security Program Managers (ISSPM)
Agency IRM, Automation Information System Management, Operations and Programming Staff
All USDA agencies and staff offices
USDA, OMB, NIST and other governing bodies
employees, contractors, volunteers, partners, or customers
agency ISSPM, Deputy ISSPM and ISSM/ISSO positions
US-CERT and other computer emergency response teams
agency IT Program Managers and ISSPM (ISSM or ISSO as appropriate)

policy_statements.source_text: On January 23, 2002, Congress enacted Public Law, 107-347, E-Government Act of 2002.

The Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002, Title III, of this law requires that each agency have effective information security controls over Information Technology (IT) to support Federal operations and assets and provide a mechanism for improved oversight of Federal agency information security programs.
cross_references: Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002, Title III

policy_statements.source_text: This Act was designed to strengthen OMB Circular A-130, Appendix III that initially established specific requirements for all agency security programs.
As technology has grown more complex and open, the need for effective Federal information security programs in each agency and staff office is essential.
In USDA, this program is referred to as the Information Systems Security Program (ISSP).
USDA has undertaken an aggressive role in support of E-gov to include ensuring that IT systems have been certified and accredited or otherwise authorized as being properly secured.
All of these actions require that each agency ISSP be responsive and responsible in supporting security requirements.

The material in this chapter is designed to outline the responsibilities of each agency and staff office ISSP and to specifically define the security roles of the Agency Administrator or Head, Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM).
policy_statements.target: each agency and staff office ISSP

policy_statements.source_text: These positions are vital components in securing USDA corporate information technology assets by providing effective agency management and oversight of its ISSP.
All USDA agencies and staff offices will organize, implement and maintain an ISSP that ensures security of all information technology assets.
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA agencies and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Security must be adequately addressed in all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC), normally commencing in the IT System Initiation Phase.
conditions: in all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC), normally commencing in the IT System Initiation Phase

policy_statements.source_text: Each agency ISSP will include the following responsibilities:
Categorize sensitivity of information and information systems in accordance with FIPS 199;
policy_statements.target: sensitivity of information and information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct regular risk assessments for IT systems and computing devices;
Implement effective risk mitigation strategies;
Conduct formal Certification and Accreditation (C&A) of all agency IT systems;
Implement security controls throughout the System Life Cycle;
Use the Capital Planning and Investment Controls (CPIC) process to formulate and plan security costs for all systems;
policy_statements.target: Capital Planning and Investment Controls (CPIC) process

policy_statements.source_text: Monitor the system Configuration Management (CM) process of all systems;
Prepare agency annual Program and System Specific Security Plans;
policy_statements.target: agency annual Program and System Specific Security Plans

policy_statements.source_text: Manage an effective Security Awareness and Training Program;
policy_statements.target: effective Security Awareness and Training Program

policy_statements.source_text: Manage the agency Security Incident Response Program;
Conduct annual self-assessment of the ISSP using NIST 800-26 and NIST 800-53;
Monitor IT systems using audit trails, controls logs and other mechanisms;
Establish an electronic inventory of all IT systems and computing devices;
policy_statements.target: electronic inventory of all IT systems and computing devices

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain agency IT inventory in the Enterprise Architecture Repository (EAR);
Disseminate department policy and procedures to all agency personnel;
Respond to regular and ad hoc reporting requirements and audits by internal or external agencies; and
policy_statements.target: regular and ad hoc reporting requirements and audits

policy_statements.source_text: Monitor agency compliance to USDA, OMB, NIST and other governing bodies’ policy for security.

Agencies may elect either a traditional ISSP structure with the responsibilities delineated in Responsibilities, Section 4, of this policy or use the alternative structure defined in Procedures, Section 3 below.

An alternative structure is useful in agencies of greater than 1,000 IT users (employees, contractors, volunteers, partners, or customers), as it outlines the tactical security responsibilities below the ISSPM level.
conditions: in agencies of greater than 1,000 IT users (employees, contractors, volunteers, partners, or customers)

policy_statements.source_text: The duties of the ISSPM/ISSM can be designated as the agency sees fit, as long as all responsibilities are designated in writing and effectively executed.
conditions: as long as all responsibilities are designated in writing and effectively executed

policy_statements.source_text: Associate CIO for Cyber Security (ACIO CS) must be advised that the alternative structure is being implemented and each agency must comply with the duties defined for this structure.

Each Agency Head or CIO will formally designate at least one Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM) using the Designation of ISSPM and Deputy ISSPM_form contained in Appendix A to serve in these positions.
policy_statements.target: at least one Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)
cross_references: Designation of ISSPM and Deputy ISSPM_form

policy_statements.source_text: These forms will be sent to the ACIO CS when individuals are assigned to these positions.
conditions: when individuals are assigned to these positions

policy_statements.source_text: The duties and responsibilities of an ISSPM are diverse, comprehensive and complex.
policy_statements.target: duties and responsibilities of an ISSPM

policy_statements.source_text: This position is one of high sensitivity and level of trust and therefore will be filled only by full time government personnel.
In addition, this position has a requirement for high confidentiality due to the critical nature of the investigatory and compliance work.
Therefore space should be assigned to the ISSPM and Deputy ISSPM that affords locking files and the ability to conduct meetings of a highly sensitive nature in private.
In no case, are ISSPMs and Deputy ISSPMs to be assigned to a work/office area with individuals not associated with information security.
conditions: In no case

policy_statements.source_text: To successfully establish, manage and improve an agency/staff office/program area ISSP, the ISSPM shall receive comprehensive annual security training.
Agencies/staff offices/program areas shall appoint a Deputy ISSPM and as many Information Systems Security Officers (ISSOs) as necessary to comply with this policy.
policy_statements.target: Deputy ISSPM and as many Information Systems Security Officers (ISSOs)
conditions: as necessary to comply with this policy

policy_statements.source_text: The agency ISSPM shall be recognized as the organization’s CS expert, leader and point of contact.
policy_statements.resulting_status: organization’s CS expert, leader and point of contact

policy_statements.source_text: The agency ISSPM, Deputy ISSPM and ISSM/ISSO positions are considered to be High Risk Public Trust positions as defined by 5 CFR 731.
policy_statements.target: agency ISSPM, Deputy ISSPM and ISSM/ISSO positions

policy_statements.source_text: Each agency will ensure that the individuals in these positions have the appropriate level of background investigation completed.
Additionally, each agency is responsible for determining the National Defense sensitivity level of these positions as defined in 5 CFR 732 and obtaining the appropriate level of security clearance.
policy_statements.target: National Defense sensitivity level of these positions

policy_statements.source_text: Individuals in these positions will have a direct reporting relationship with the agency CIO.
Policy Exception Requirements – Agencies/Staff Offices and program areas that cannot comply with this policy will submit all policy exception requests directly to the ACIO CS.
conditions: that cannot comply with this policy

policy_statements.source_text: Temporary exceptions to policy will be considered only in terms of implementation timeframes and progress toward meeting the standards will be monitored by OCIO CS.

Exceptions that are approved will require that each agency report this Granted Policy Exception (GPE) as a Plan of Action & Milestone (POA&M) in their FISMA reporting, with a GPE notation, until full compliance is achieved.
conditions: that are approved
until full compliance is achieved

policy_statements.source_text: Interim exceptions expire with each fiscal year.
conditions: with each fiscal year

policy_statements.source_text: Compliance exceptions that require longer durations will be considered for renewal on an annual basis with an updated timeline for completion.
conditions: that require longer durations
on an annual basis with an updated timeline for completion

policy_statements.source_text: OCIO CS will monitor all approved exceptions.
Agencies and staff offices electing to adopt a three-tier ISSP management approach will have a structure comprised of:
conditions: electing to adopt a three-tier ISSP management approach

policy_statements.source_text: Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM): This person and the deputy ISSPM are responsible for managing the ISS efforts for an entire agency or staff office.
policy_statements.target: ISS efforts for an entire agency or staff office

policy_statements.source_text: This person is a program manager responsible for the strategic security requirements of the program to include planning, budget review, consolidation of agency security reports, and coordination of the ISSP into the culture of the entire organization.
policy_statements.target: strategic security requirements of the program

policy_statements.source_text: ISSPMs will act as consultants for ISSM/ISSOs and work with them to resolve highly technical matters, when necessary.
conditions: when necessary

policy_statements.source_text: Ultimately, the ISSPM is still responsible for efficient operation of the overall ISSP.
policy_statements.target: efficient operation of the overall ISSP

policy_statements.source_text: Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM): This individual(s), including deputy(ies), is responsible for managing the tactical efforts of a business, functional, or operational entity within an agency.
policy_statements.target: tactical efforts of a business, functional, or operational entity within an agency

policy_statements.source_text: Their responsibilities include the daily operational security issues of the unit and overall management of the “front line” security requirements for the unit.
policy_statements.target: daily operational security issues of the unit and overall management of the “front line” security requirements for the unit

policy_statements.source_text: This individual may often be called upon to assist in the resolution of certain system security issues.
policy_statements.target: resolution of certain system security issues

policy_statements.source_text: Information Systems Security Officer (ISSO): This person(s), including deputy(ies), is responsible for the day-to-day security administration for one or more information systems.
policy_statements.target: day-to-day security administration for one or more information systems

policy_statements.source_text: Theirs is an operational security effort regarding the system(s) for which they are responsible.
policy_statements.target: system(s) for which they are responsible

policy_statements.source_text: The Agency Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Act as the agency Senior Security Officer (SSO) who is responsible for supporting the strategic requirements of the ISSP;
Ensure that adequate funding, training and resources are provided to the ISSP to support the agency mission;
Facilitate the resolution of high-level security matters within the agency by acting as a champion for the ISSPM;
policy_statements.target: resolution of high-level security matters within the agency

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that ISSM/ISSOs are designated to provide adequate security to business, functional or operational entities;

Serve as the certification official for agency security requirements (i.e., Annual Security Plans, FISMA and other formal reporting requirements, Waiver Requests and Certification of agency IT Systems);

Formally designate in writing to ACIO CS the ISSPM(s) and Deputy(ies) for each agency; ensure that these individuals are permanent members of all system development, telecommunications planning and System Development Life Cycle planning teams; and
Provide role-based and specialized security-based training to the ISSPM(s) and Deputy ISSPM(s) from USDA enterprise training vehicles.
The Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM) will:
Manage the agency ISSP including the activities and training from USDA Enterprise training vehicles of the ISSM/ISSOs;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)

policy_statements.source_text: Support the strategic security program requirements to include: planning, budget analysis, department policy review and internal policy formulation, agency FISMA, POA&M, and audit reporting requirements, agency Security Architecture and agency IT CPIC;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)

policy_statements.source_text: Consolidate individual reports from all functional and operation units into one agency combined report (i.e., monthly scans, patches, incidents) for higher level management, including ACIO CS;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)
policy_statements.target: individual reports from all functional and operation units

policy_statements.source_text: Monitor the progress of the ISSM/ISSOs to ensure that they meet the necessary program security requirements of NIST 800-26 and departmental policy directives;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)

policy_statements.source_text: Serves as the principle consultant to the agency CIO and senior management, including ACIO CS;
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate agency Incident Response with the agency ISSM/ISSOs to include all associated actions necessary to mitigate the risk to unit systems; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee the implementation of agency security policies, procedures and guidelines.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)
policy_statements.target: implementation of agency security policies, procedures and guidelines

policy_statements.source_text: The Agency Information Systems Security Manager (ISSM) will:
Serve as the Point of Contact (POC) for all unit CS matters; provide subject matter guidance to agency personnel;
Participate in the process and monitor to ensure that all agency systems are C&A’d prior to actual operation and that they are reaccredited every three years or when significant system change occurs;
conditions: prior to actual operation
every three years or when significant system change occurs

policy_statements.source_text: Disseminate departmental security policy and procedures; formulate internal agency security procedures and support implementation, testing, and integration into the agency culture (mission and business operation);
Participate as a permanent member of unit system development teams, telecommunications planning, and System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) processes;
policy_statements.target: unit system development teams, telecommunications planning, and System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) processes

policy_statements.source_text: Conduct internal audits of all agency IT systems to ensure compliance with federal and departmental policy and procedures;
Participate in general and role-based security training to enhance knowledge and skill level; recommend appropriate training for staff to ISSPM;

Proactively coordinate the establishment of system security controls to protect agency information using authentication techniques, encryption, firewalls, access controls, and comprehensive departmental Incident Response Procedures with all System Administrators (SA) and business owners;
Coordinate with business owners to categorize information systems and determine sensitivity levels;
Establish Disaster Recovery/Business Resumption (DR/BR) and other emergency plans for all IT systems; ensure compliance with backup and storage procedures;
policy_statements.target: Disaster Recovery/Business Resumption (DR/BR) and other emergency plans

policy_statements.source_text: Monitor physical spaces to ensure that the security requirements of IT Restricted Space are followed in maintaining, updating or planning new space, and advise the CIO if space does not meet security requirements;
conditions: if space does not meet security requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Develop and manage a Security Awareness Program including arranging or conducting security awareness briefings; recommend to the agency ISSPM security training for all agency personnel, including contractors, based on their role in the organization; ensure that all personnel are appropriately trained in the security Rules of Behavior prior to being granted access to unit systems;
conditions: based on their role in the organization
prior to being granted access to unit systems

policy_statements.source_text: Arrange for background screening of unit employees based on the level of trust and sensitivity of the position they occupy in the organization;
conditions: based on the level of trust and sensitivity of the position they occupy in the organization

policy_statements.source_text: Participate in the development of an agency security architecture for all IT systems;
Monitor and coordinate patch management and scanning techniques for all unit systems; participate in identification and mitigation of all system vulnerabilities,
Coordinate the provision of security controls for Portable Electronic Devices (PEDS) and other wireless technology;
policy_statements.target: security controls for Portable Electronic Devices (PEDS) and other wireless technology

policy_statements.source_text: Participate in the Overall Agency Security Plan for the program and coordinate with Information Systems Security Officers (ISSO) to ensure that current system specific plans are in place for all IT systems; coordinate or participate in risk assessments of all unit systems and mitigate vulnerabilities;
Monitor CM practices to ensure that security controls are maintained over the life of the IT systems, and formulate and prepare an electronic agency inventory for unit computing devices;
Monitor and participate in assessments to ensure that Privacy requirements are met;
Plan and document security costs for unit IT investments and systems;
Prepare and update reports to ensure that the unit complies with mandated internal and external security reporting requirements, including FISMA and CPIC;
Proactively participate in new CS initiatives including, but not limited to, computer investigations and forensics; and
Prepare and coordinate unit Incident Responses with the agency ISSPM to include all associated actions necessary to mitigate the risk to unit systems.
Agency Information Systems Security Officers (ISSO) will:
Be knowledgeable of Federal, Departmental, and agency security regulations when developing functional and technical requirements; serve as a POC for system users with security issues;
conditions: when developing functional and technical requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate security program and system elements with the agency IT Program Managers by evaluating system environments for security requirements and controls including: IT Security Architecture, hardware, software, telecommunications, security trends, and associated threats and vulnerabilities;

Manage security controls to ensure confidentiality, integrity and availability of information; build security into the system development process and define security specifications to support the acquisition of new systems; review and sign off on system procurement requests to ensure that security has been considered and included;
Assist with security controls and associated costs in the CPIC Process;

Assist the ISSM in the C&A process, including updates to the overall Agency and System Security Plans (SSP) for the program; serve as a key advisor in risk assessments of all systems and mitigate vulnerabilities; adhere to CM practices to ensure that security controls are maintained over the life of IT systems; update the electronic agency inventory for all agency computing devices;

Adhere to and implement system security controls that ensure the protection of Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU) information using authentication techniques, encryption, firewalls, and access controls;
Assist the ISSPM in following Department Incident Response Procedures;

Assist the system owner and ISSM in the development, testing and maintenance of agency and system contingency plans, backup and storage procedures; document all procedures according to departmental and agency standards;
Audit and monitor application, system and security logs for security threats, vulnerabilities and suspicious activities; report suspicious activities to the agency ISSPM;
Support and facilitate the security awareness, training and education program; and
policy_statements.target: security awareness, training and education program

On January 23, 2002, Congress enacted Public Law, 107-347, E-Government Act of 2002.

The Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002, Title III, of this law requires that each agency have effective information security controls over Information Technology (IT) to support Federal operations and assets and provide a mechanism for improved oversight of Federal agency information security programs.
Federal Information Security Management Act (FISMA) of 2002, Title III
This Act was designed to strengthen OMB Circular A-130, Appendix III that initially established specific requirements for all agency security programs.
As technology has grown more complex and open, the need for effective Federal information security programs in each agency and staff office is essential.
In USDA, this program is referred to as the Information Systems Security Program (ISSP).
USDA has undertaken an aggressive role in support of E-gov to include ensuring that IT systems have been certified and accredited or otherwise authorized as being properly secured.
All of these actions require that each agency ISSP be responsive and responsible in supporting security requirements.

The material in this chapter is designed to outline the responsibilities of each agency and staff office ISSP and to specifically define the security roles of the Agency Administrator or Head, Chief Information Officer (CIO) and Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM).
each agency and staff office ISSP
These positions are vital components in securing USDA corporate information technology assets by providing effective agency management and oversight of its ISSP.
All USDA agencies and staff offices will organize, implement and maintain an ISSP that ensures security of all information technology assets.
All USDA agencies and staff offices

All USDA agencies and staff offices will organize, implement and maintain an ISSP that ensures security of all information technology assets. Security must be adequately addressed in all phases of the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC), normally
Each agency ISSP will include the following responsibilities:
Categorize sensitivity of information and information systems in accordance with FIPS 199;
Conduct regular risk assessments for IT systems and computing devices;
Conduct formal Certification and Accreditation (C&A) of all agency IT systems;
Implement security controls throughout the System Life Cycle;
Use the Capital Planning and Investment Controls (CPIC) process to formulate and plan security costs for all systems;
Monitor the system Configuration Management (CM) process of all systems;
Prepare agency annual Program and System Specific Security Plans;
Manage an effective Security Awareness and Training Program;
Manage the agency Security Incident Response Program;
Conduct annual self-assessment of the ISSP using NIST 800-26 and NIST 800-53;
Monitor IT systems using audit trails, controls logs and other mechanisms;
Establish an electronic inventory of all IT systems and computing devices;
Maintain agency IT inventory in the Enterprise Architecture Repository (EAR);
Disseminate department policy and procedures to all agency personnel;
Respond to regular and ad hoc reporting requirements and audits by internal or external agencies; and
Monitor agency compliance to USDA, OMB, NIST and other governing bodies’ policy for security.

Agencies may elect either a traditional ISSP structure with the responsibilities delineated in Responsibilities, Section 4, of this policy or use the alternative structure defined in Procedures, Section 3 below.

Agencies may elect either a traditional ISSP structure with the responsibilities delineated in Responsibilities, Section 4, of this policy or use the alternative structure defined in Procedures, Section 3 below. in agencies of greater than 1,000 IT users (employees, contractors, volunteers, partners, or customers)
The duties of the ISSPM/ISSM can be designated as the agency sees fit, as long as all responsibilities are designated in writing and effectively executed.
as long as all responsibilities are designated in writing and effectively executed
Associate CIO for Cyber Security (ACIO CS) must be advised that the alternative structure is being implemented and each agency must comply with the duties defined for this structure.

Each Agency Head or CIO will formally designate at least one Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM) using the Designation of ISSPM and Deputy ISSPM_form contained in Appendix A to serve in these positions.
at least one Information Systems Security Program Manager (ISSPM)
Designation of ISSPM and Deputy ISSPM_form
These forms will be sent to the ACIO CS when individuals are assigned to these positions.
when individuals are assigned to these positions
The duties and responsibilities of an ISSPM are diverse, comprehensive and complex.
duties and responsibilities of an ISSPM
This position is one of high sensitivity and level of trust and therefore will be filled only by full time government personnel.
In addition, this position has a requirement for high confidentiality due to the critical nature of the investigatory and compliance work.
Therefore space should be assigned to the ISSPM and Deputy ISSPM that affords locking files and the ability to conduct meetings of a highly sensitive nature in private.
In no case, are ISSPMs and Deputy ISSPMs to be assigned to a work/office area with individuals not associated with information security.
To successfully establish, manage and improve an agency/staff office/program area ISSP, the ISSPM shall receive comprehensive annual security training.
Agencies/staff offices/program areas shall appoint a Deputy ISSPM and as many Information Systems Security Officers (ISSOs) as necessary to comply with this policy.
Deputy ISSPM and as many Information Systems Security Officers (ISSOs)
as necessary to comply with this policy
The agency ISSPM shall be recognized as the organization’s CS expert, leader and point of contact.
organization’s CS expert, leader and point of contact
The agency ISSPM, Deputy ISSPM and ISSM/ISSO positions are considered to be High Risk Public Trust positions as defined by 5 CFR 731.
agency ISSPM, Deputy ISSPM and ISSM/ISSO positions
Each agency will ensure that the individuals in these positions have the appropriate level of background investigation completed.
Additionally, each agency is responsible for determining the National Defense sensitivity level of these positions as defined in 5 CFR 732 and obtaining the appropriate level of security clearance.
National Defense sensitivity level of these positions
Individuals in these positions will have a direct reporting relationship with the agency CIO.
Policy Exception Requirements  – Agencies/Staff Offices and program areas that cannot comply with this policy will submit all policy exception requests directly to the ACIO CS.
that cannot comply with this policy
Temporary exceptions to policy will be considered only in terms of implementation timeframes and progress toward meeting the standards will be monitored by OCIO CS.

Exceptions that are approved will require that each agency report this Granted Policy Exception (GPE) as a Plan of Action & Milestone (POA&M) in their FISMA reporting, with a GPE notation, until full compliance is achieved.
Interim exceptions expire with each fiscal year.
Compliance exceptions that require longer durations will be considered for renewal on an annual basis with an updated timeline for completion.
on an annual basis with an updated timeline for completion
